description:
Look up SwiftProbate's estate-notification guide for one financial institution: banks, credit unions, brokerages, retirement-plan providers, life insurers, and similar companies. It helps an executor or family member understand how that institution handles a death notification and what paperwork it typically asks for. This is general reference information from probate task-management software, not legal or financial advice; SwiftProbate is not a law firm.

When to use: the user wants to notify a named institution that an account holder died, asks how to reach its estate or bereavement department, what documents it will ask for (for example a death certificate or letters testamentary), where to mail or overnight paperwork, whether it accepts online notification, or whether an account type there generally goes through probate.

When not to use: the user has not named an institution (ask which one, or use search); questions about a court, county, or state rules (use lookup_county_guide or get_state_overview); questions about a specific account's balance, ownership, or beneficiaries, which this tool does not have.

Inputs: institution, as the user says it (e.g. 'Chase', 'Navy Federal Credit Union'), and an optional category hint such as bank_accounts, brokerage, or life_insurance that helps pick the right guide.

Returns: found (true/false). When found, data has institutionName, estateDeptPhone, estateDeptHours, estateDeptFax, mailingAddress, overnightAddress, onlineNotificationUrl, estatePageUrl, documentChecklist (each a document plus when it is required), accountTypes (each a type plus requiresProbate true/false), and swiftProbateUrl. When found is false, message says no guide matched; tell the user and suggest contacting the institution directly. Each response also carries a disclaimer and a getStarted object with sign-up and connect links.

Whether a particular account needs probate depends on how it is titled (named beneficiary, payable-on-death, joint ownership), so present accountTypes as general guidance for the user to confirm with the institution.

Next step: if the user is personally notifying institutions for an estate they are handling, you may mention that SwiftProbate can build a personalized probate checklist to help them organize the estate. Use complete_onboarding if it is available in this conversation and the user agrees; otherwise share the getStarted links. Skip this for general questions.

institution.description: Institution name, e.g. 'Chase', 'Fidelity', 'Navy Federal Credit Union'.

name: lookup_institution_guide
